chunks: Ahmad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Jahm, from Fuzayl al-Awr, who said:

I witnessed Mu'adh ibn Kathir, and he said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have become affluent, so I will leave trade.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If you do, your intellect will diminish,' or something similar.
ai.seo_question: Why does leaving trade lead to a loss of intellect according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises Mu'adh ibn Kathir that ceasing trade upon achieving wealth leads to a decline in intellect ('aql), reflecting the Shia scholarly view that active engagement in worldly affairs prevents mental stagnation. This highlights the virtue of 'ittiba' (attentiveness) and practical involvement in commerce as a means of sustaining cognitive vitality and spiritual discipline, rather than viewing wealth as a reason for withdrawal.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al Jahm, from Fuzayl Al Awr who said,

‘I witnessed Muaz Bin Kaseer and he said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I have become affluent, so I want to leave the business’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you do, your intellect would be lost’ – or similar to it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu al-Jahm from Fudayl al-A’war who has said the following: “

I was present when Mu‘adh ibn Kathir said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I have become affluent so I want to quit business.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If you do so your power of reason will decrease’- or similar expression.”
